OBLAK
DeviceServicesInstallationChecks
Private home server · always on

A small box.
Your own cloud.

OBLAK is a compact Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 home server for files, photos, music, movies and private services. It is designed to stay connected, quietly, on a wall, shelf or desk.

32 GB eMMC2 TB NVMePassive cooling 3.52″ e-paperEthernet + USB-C
01 · The object

One device.
Three places.

These renders define the visual direction: compact proportions, translucent dusty-pink enclosure, a small pink e-paper window, soft rounded ends and no oversized desktop-computer appearance.

The device is always connected with two cables: Ethernet and USB-C power. The screen stays at roughly one quarter of the device width.
01

Wall

Mount it near the network connection. Keep the two cables routed cleanly downward or behind the enclosure.

02

Shelf

Let it stand as a small piece of domestic hardware with the e-paper status display visible.

03

Desk

Place it next to a workstation and use its storage and web services over the local network.

ComputeRaspberry Pi CM5 · 32 GB eMMC

02 · What OBLAK does

Your home,
on one box.

Linux underneath, simple services above it. OBLAK becomes the central storage and application node while music and DNS can remain on their dedicated Raspberry Pis.

N

Storage

NFS and Samba expose shared storage. WebDAV and Filebrowser can provide controlled remote access.

M

Media

Jellyfin handles movies and media. Navidrome deliberately remains on the separate music Pi.

P

Private access

WireGuard provides remote access while UFW and fail2ban reduce the exposed attack surface.

03 · Installation

Build it in
six phases.

The original twelve steps are grouped here so the installation follows the physical logic of the machine: hardware → boot → storage → security → services → display and testing.

01

Hardware & first boot

Prepare the CM5, flash eMMC and establish the network identity.

Hardware

CM5 32 GB eMMC · IO board/carrier · 2 TB NVMe · passive heatsink · Waveshare 3.52″ e-paper + Raw Panel Driver HAT · Ethernet · USB-C power.

USB boot & flash

Put the CM5 into USB boot mode and connect it to another computer.

rpiboot
Raspberry Pi Imager

Choose Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit), target the CM5 eMMC. Set hostname oblak, enable SSH and add your key.

First login
ssh <user>@oblak.local
sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y
Network identity: reserve <oblak-ip> for OBLAK in the router DHCP settings.
02

Base system

Enable the hardware interfaces and apply the basic SSH/system settings.

/boot/firmware/config.txt

dtparam=spi=on
dtparam=act_led_trigger=default-on
dtoverlay=gpio-shutdown

CPU governor

echo powersave | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor

SSH hardening — in /etc/ssh/sshd_config:

PermitRootLogin no
X11Forwarding no

sudo systemctl restart ssh
03

NVMe storage & Docker

Put the working data and Docker data-root on the 2 TB NVMe.

Important: mkfs.ext4 erases the selected device. Run lsblk first and verify that /dev/nvme0n1 is the intended SSD.
sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/nvme0n1
sudo mkdir /OBLAK
sudo mount /dev/nvme0n1 /OBLAK
echo '/dev/nvme0n1  /OBLAK  ext4  defaults  0  2' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
sudo mkdir -p /OBLAK/Programi/docker /OBLAK/Share

Install Docker

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

/etc/docker/daemon.json

{
  "data-root": "/OBLAK/Programi/docker",
  "dns": ["<oblak-ip>"],
  "ipv6": false
}
sudo systemctl restart docker
04

Network security

Lock down incoming traffic before exposing any remote service.

UFW
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw default allow outgoing
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw route allow routed
sudo ufw enable
fail2ban
sudo apt install fail2ban -y
sudo systemctl enable --now fail2ban
WireGuard
sudo apt install wireguard -y
wg genkey | tee privatekey | wg pubkey > publickey
/etc/wireguard/wg0.conf
[Interface]
Address = 10.9.0.1/24
ListenPort = 51820
PrivateKey = <server private key>

[Peer]
PublicKey = <client public key>
AllowedIPs = 10.9.0.x/32
sudo systemctl enable --now wg-quick@wg0
router: forward UDP 51820 to OBLAK. Disable unnecessary outward exposure such as UPnP, WPS and remote administration. Verify externally that only the intended port is visible.
05

Core services & remote sharing

Start the application stack and keep music/DNS on their dedicated Pis.

Create /OBLAK/Programi/docker/docker-compose.yml with Immich, Jellyfin, Homepage, Portainer, Kavita and Samba:

Show Docker Compose file 
services:
  immich:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:release
    ports: ["2283:2283"]
    volumes: ["/OBLAK/Photos:/usr/src/app/upload"]
    restart: unless-stopped

  jellyfin:
    image: jellyfin/jellyfin
    ports: ["8096:8096"]
    volumes: ["/OBLAK/Media:/media"]
    restart: unless-stopped

  homepage:
    image: ghcr.io/gethomepage/homepage
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
    volumes:
      - /etc/homepage:/app/config
      - /etc/homepage/icons/apple-touch-icon.png:/app/public/apple-touch-icon.png:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /OBLAK:/OBLAK:ro
    restart: unless-stopped

  portainer:
    image: portainer/portainer-ce
    ports: ["9443:9443"]
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - portainer_data:/data

  kavita:
    image: kizaing/kavita
    ports: ["5000:5000"]
    volumes: ["/OBLAK/Books:/books"]

  samba:
    image: dperson/samba
    ports: ["445:445"]
    volumes: ["/OBLAK/Share:/share"]

volumes:
  portainer_data:
cd /OBLAK/Programi/docker && docker compose up -d
Architecture choice: NFS runs on the host via nfs-kernel-server. Navidrome and Pi-hole stay on their own Pis so an OBLAK restart does not interrupt music or DNS.
WebDAV + Filebrowser

Build Caddy with WebDAV, Cloudflare DNS and Dynamic DNS modules:

xcaddy build \
  --with github.com/mholt/caddy-webdav \
  --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare \
  --with github.com/mholt/caddy-dynamicdns

For controlled Filebrowser exposure:

caddy hash-password

# share-on
sudo ufw allow 8443/tcp
docker start filebrowser

# share-off
sudo ufw delete allow 8443/tcp
docker stop filebrowser
06

E-paper display, backups & final check

Finish the physical interface, verify the machine and establish recovery routines.

E-paper DIP switches: Display = A · Interface = 0.

git clone https://github.com/waveshareteam/e-Paper.git
cd e-Paper/RaspberryPi_JetsonNano/python/examples
python3 epd_3in52_test.py

Persistent display service:

[Unit]
Description=oblak e-paper display
After=network.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /home/<user>/epapper.py
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
sudo systemctl enable --now epapper.service
Render portrait at 240×360 and rotate into the native 360×240 framebuffer. Use lut_DU for fast updates and a periodic lut_GC pass to clear ghosting. The screen can show TEMP / CPU / RAM / DISK and switch to cover art when music plays.
Backup routine 
rsync -a /OBLAK/ <backup-host>:<backup-path>/
ssh <backup-host> "dd if=/dev/mmcblk0 bs=4M | gzip" \
  > sdcard_$(date +%F).img.gz
PIPE_STATUS=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")

Weekly timer:

[Timer]
OnCalendar=Thu 02:00
Persistent=true
04 · Final check

Ready when all six
checks pass.

docker ps — containers are Up
sudo ufw status verbose — default deny
sudo wg show — peer + recent handshake
systemctl list-timers | grep backup — backup timer present
curl -I http://oblak:3000 — Homepage responds
stress-ng --cpu 4 --timeout 60s — no throttling

At idle, the system should hold roughly in the mid-40s °C without throttling. Once installed, OBLAK is intended to stay powered and connected rather than being switched on and off like a conventional computer.
